examples: Why will my bulb not light?

groups.ask: Why will my bulb not light?

explain.say: Your torch will not light up. Oh no! Time to be a circuit detective. A circuit is a loop that electricity flows around. Look at the board: some circuits light the bulb and some do not. Let's find out why.

explain.say: Here is a real circuit: a battery, a switch, a bulb, and wires joining them in a loop. See the bulb lighting up? Electricity flows from the battery, along the wire, through the bulb, and back to the battery. Can you trace the loop with your finger?
Now see Bulb lights glow. The bulb lights only with a complete loop, a closed switch and a battery with energy left. Complete means no gaps anywhere. What do you think happens if a wire comes loose?

explain.say: Here is Bulb stays dark. A gap in a wire, an open switch, a flat battery or a loose bulb all break the circuit, so electricity cannot flow round. Which would you check first in your torch?

groups.label: Bulb stays dark
groups.ask: Why will my bulb not light?

explain.say: And that switch? See it light up. A switch is a gap you can open and close on purpose: closed, the loop is complete and the bulb shines; open, it goes dark. Super detective work! Wow fact: the word circuit comes from circle, because electricity must go all the way round.

faq.a: A complete circuit is an unbroken loop from one end of the battery, through the wires and components like a bulb, and back to the other end. Electricity can only flow when the loop is complete.

faq.q: Why will my bulb not light?
faq.a: Look for a break in the loop: a loose or broken wire, an open switch, a loose or broken bulb, or a flat battery. Fix the gap and the bulb should light.
asks: Why does my circuit not work?

faq.a: A switch opens and closes a gap in the circuit. When it is closed, the metal parts touch and electricity flows; when it is open, the gap stops the flow.

faq.q: What does a battery do in a circuit?
faq.a: A battery pushes electricity around the circuit and gives it energy, which the bulb turns into light and heat. A flat battery has used up its energy.
asks: Why do circuits need a battery?

faq.q: Is it safe to experiment with circuits?
faq.a: Small batteries like AA cells are safe for experiments. Never play with plugs, sockets or mains electricity, which can kill.
asks: Can I test circuits at home?

facts: Current flows only when there is a complete, unbroken loop in a circuit.
The word circuit comes from the Latin circuitus, meaning going around.

quiz.show: With one wire not touching, the bulb…
quiz.why: The gap breaks the loop, so no electricity flows and the bulb stays dark.

wrong.0: A bulb needs a complete loop to light.
wrong.2: With a gap, there is no flow at all, so no flashing either.

quiz.say: What does a switch do when it is open?

options.show: Makes a gap in the circuit
options.say: Makes a gap in the circuit

quiz.why: An open switch makes a gap, so the electricity stops flowing.

wrong.2: An open switch turns the bulb off, not brighter.
